2. The petitioner filed the above case under section 96 of - the State Acquisition - and Tenancy Act seeking preemption of the land measuring 1.98 acres stating, inter alia, that Ishwar Chandra Dey' and Prahallad Chandra Dey were the C.S. recorded tenants of Plot No. 5111 appearing to C.S. khatian No.96 and they possessed the same in equal shares, Prahalled offered fiz  sell .73 acres of land to the petitioner and, upon receiving Tk.700/-as part of the consideration Prahallad executed baina and also handed over possession of .73 acres of land to the petitioner but Prahallad having died before execution and registration of the sale deed, the petitioner filed Title Suit No.248 of 1968- for specific performance of contract and after obtaining decree on 6.3.1969 he got the deed executed and registered on 1.3.1971 through Title Execution Case No.03 of 197 I and thus became a co-sharer by purchase and that linnet Ali, the opposite party No. I of the preemption case is a stranger in the said Khatian and on 6.5.1972 he purchased 3,79 acres of land from the said Khatian from other two co-sharers- namely. Kushum Kamini Datta and Makhan Bala. Datta, opposite party respondent Nos. 11 and 12 and that the said opposite parties:No.11 and 12 sold the said land to the opposite party No. I without serving any notice upon the petitioner and as such the petitioner is entitled to get preemption of the land. The opposite parties contested the case by tiling written objection contending, inter aka, that the case is barred by limitation, the petitioner is not a co-sharer of the case holding. the case land being harnessed in nature and situated within the municipal area of .Sherpur Town is not preempt able under Section 90 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Kushum Kamini Datta, the vendor of the deed under preemption, is not a co-sharer of the case holding and even Prahallad, the predecessor of the petitioner, had no interest in the case holding and the preemptor-petitioner has no right to get the case holding by way of preemption. 

 4. The learned counsel -appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division failed to take into considerali0ii that the land under C.S. Khatian No. 96 was recorded in S. A. Khatian Nos. 326 and 327 and the petitioner on- 4.3.1971 became co-sharer of the same on the basis of purchase from the Prahallad, the C. S. recorded tenant, in whose name the said S.A. Khatian also stood and so the petitioner being a co-Sharer in the said holding had right to get the case land on preemption and it is evident from the contents of the judgment of the High Court Division that the names of Makhan Bala Data and Prahallad Dey, were recorded as tenants in S.A. Khatian No. 326 which is also evident item Exhibit 1(a) and an the High Court Division ,committed error in holding -that the Khatian being found already separated before the sale, the preemptor even if had interest in the C.S. holding is not entitled to get preemption in as much as the petitioner having entered into the shoes of his vendor in the S.A. Khatian No.326 became a co-sharer tenant in the said S.A. Khatian No.326. The learned counsel further submits that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration the fact that S.A. record of the area concerned was finally published in the year 1962-63 and the petitioner became co-sharer of the case holding by purchase on 1.3.1971 and so there was no scope of that the trial court wrongly and erroneously found that the petitioner is not a co-sharer of the case holding in spite of the fact that the petitioner purchased the suit land from the C.S. and S.A. recorded tenant of the case holding and he being a co-sharer by purchase has the right to get the case land by preemption and accordingly the appellate court below correctly sent back the case on remand to the trial court for proper adjudication of the case and in accordance with the provisions of Order 41 Rule23 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. As it appears the High Court fraud that the case land being situated within the Sherpur Municipality preemption was not available tinder section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and during the hearing of Miscellaneous 'Appeal. No. 20 of 11052 the above wrong .being detected the suit was sent back remand and then the original application for preemption was amended on 273;1983 and the trial court on 28.6. 1984 passed the second judgment treating the application under section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act and that plaint or application is allowed to be amended it takes effect from the date of filing of the original plaint or application and therefore the point of limitation can no eager be raised and as such the learned Assistant Judge wrongly decided the point of limitation and that the admitted position being that the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer tenant in the two S.A. Khatian out of which the case land was transferred, he cannot get order of preemption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act as the Khatian being found already separated before the sale, the preemptor, even if had interest in the C.S. holding, is not entitled to get preemption and accordingly the remand order, as has been passed by the appellate court, suffers from serious legal infirmity calling for interference in the revisional, jurisdiction.
